text:
A low-carbohydrate intake depletes glycogen stores and impairs high-intensity exercise, since fat oxidation cannot supply ATP fast enough to meet glycolytic demand. It may aid weight loss and promote fat oxidation in some individuals, but can cause short-term side effects and, if sustained, risks inadequate fiber and micronutrient intake unless carefully planned. Overall, it can suit specific goals but requires monitoring for nutritional adequacy and individual tolerance.
